result.title: [Troubleshoot]: RoboTwin Evaluation failure with pi05 model on official Docker image
result.body:
### Problem description

I am using the official Docker image docker.1ms.run/rlinf/rlinf:agentic-rlinf0.2-robotwin to run the RoboTwin evaluation following the documentation.
I attempted to evaluate two different models. While the OpenVLAOFT model ran successfully, the PI05 model failed. I would appreciate it if you could help check what might be causing this issue.

### Configuration YAML file

YAML config file:
based this [config](https://github.com/RLinf/RLinf/blob/main/examples/embodiment/config/robotwin_adjust_bottle_ppo_openpi_pi05.yaml) , I used my local model path and RoboTwin path.

[robotwin_adjust_bottle_ppo_openpi_pi05_custom.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26277906/robotwin_adjust_bottle_ppo_openpi_pi05_custom.yaml)



### Log file

You can find the log file in `logs/` folder or the $output_dir/$experiment_name folder (defined in the yaml config) if you are using our example scripts.

Log file:

result.title: [Bug]: user guide for the robotwin OpenPI project
result.body:
### Affected component

Could you provide a complete user guide for the robotwin OpenPI project (current documentation tends to focus on openvla-oft)? I've noticed many people in the comments section reporting bugs in the robotwin OpenPI project.

### Bug description

(EmbodiedFSDPActor pid=1406394) [INFO 08:50:22 ActorGroup-Rank-0][fsdp_model_manager.py:107] [FSDP] AMP is disabled.
(EmbodiedFSDPActor pid=1406396) [INFO 08:50:22 ActorGroup-Rank-1][fsdp_model_manager.py:107] [FSDP] AMP is disabled.
(EmbodiedFSDPActor pid=1406394) [INFO 08:51:21 ActorGroup-Rank-0][fsdp_model_manager.py:243] [FSDP] Enabling gradient checkpointing
(EmbodiedFSDPActor pid=1406396) [INFO 08:51:24 ActorGroup-Rank-1][fsdp_model_manager.py:243] [FSDP] Enabling gradient checkpointing
(EnvWorker pid=1406400) 
Exception occurred while running EnvWorker's function interact: exception is ray::EnvWorker.interact() (pid=1406400, ip=10.50.0.61, actor_id=2aef9057cae3ac4296604f3c01000000, repr=<rlinf.workers.env.env_worker.EnvWorker object at 0x78477e6b6c90>)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/mnt/nvme1/RLinf/rlinf/scheduler/worker/worker.py", line 71, in sync_func
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/mnt/nvme1/RLinf/rlinf/scheduler/worker/worker.py", line 964, in wrapper
    return func(self, *args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/mnt/nvme1/RLinf/rlinf/workers/env/env_worker.py", line 313, in interact
    self.env_list[stage_id].is_start = True
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^
IndexError: list index out of range

### Configuration YAML file

defaults:
  - env/robotwin_place_empty_cup@env.train
  - env/robotwin_place_empty_cup@env.eval
  - model/pi0@actor.model
  - training_backend/fsdp@actor.fsdp_config
  - override hydra/job_logging: stdout

hydra:
  run:
    dir: .
  output_subdir: null
  searchpath:
    - file://${oc.env:EMBODIED_PATH}/config/
    
cluster:
  num_nodes: 1
  component_placement:
    actor, env, rollout: 0-3

runner:
  task_type: embodied
  logger:
    log_path: "../results"
    project_name: rlinf
    experiment_name: "robotwin_grpo_openpi"
    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 1000
  max_steps: -1

  only_eval: True
  val_check_interval: 20
  save_interval: 20

  resume_dir: null # Optional: path to a saved checkpoint directory, such as 'checkpoints/global_step_10'. If not None, it will be used to resume training.
  ckpt_path: null  # Optional: path to a .pt checkpoint. If not None, it will be loaded after the model is instantiated (for evaluation).

algorithm:
  normalize_advantages: True
  kl_penalty: kl  # how to estimate kl divergence: kl or kl_penalty
  group_size: 8

  rollout_epoch: 8
  eval_rollout_epoch: 1 # set eval_rollout_epoch > 0 when enable runner.only_eval or runner.val_check_interval > 0

  reward_type: action_level
  logprob_type: token_level
  entropy_type: token_level

  adv_type: grpo
  loss_type: actor
  loss_agg_func: "token-mean"
  kl_beta: 0.0
  entropy_bonus: 0
  clip_ratio_high: 0.28
  clip_ratio_low: 0.2
  clip_ratio_c: 3.0
  value_clip: 0.2
  huber_delta: 10.0

  gamma: 1.0
  gae_lambda: 0.95

  reward_coef: 5.0
  filter_rewards: True
  rewards_lower_bound: 0.5
  rewards_upper_bound: 4.5

  # params for rollout
  sampling_params:
    do_sample: True
    temperature_train: 1.6
    temperature_eval: -1 # -1 means do_sample=False during evaluation
    top_k: -1
    top_p: 1.0
    repetition_penalty: 1.0

  # length argument for autoregressive sampling
  # max length means max amount of tokens to generate
  length_params:
    max_new_token: null
    max_length: 512
    min_length: 1

env:
  group_name: "EnvGroup"
  enable_offload: True

  # Override the default values in env/robotwin_place_empty_cup
  train:
    total_num_envs: 128
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_episode_steps: 200
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 200
    group_size: ${algorithm.group_size}
    assets_path: "/mnt/nvme1/chenquan/RLinf/RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/train_seeds.json
    center_crop: False
    task_config:
      embodiment: [aloha-agilex]
      camera:
        collect_wrist_camera: true
  eval:
    total_num_envs: 128
    auto_reset: True
    ignore_terminations: True
    max_episode_steps: 200
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 200
    group_size: 1
    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: True
    is_eval: True
    assets_path: "/mnt/nvme1/chenquan/RLinf/RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/eval_seeds.json
    center_crop: False
    video_cfg:
      save_video: True
      video_base_dir: ${runner.logger.log_path}/video/eval
    task_config:
      embodiment: [aloha-agilex]
      camera:
        collect_wrist_camera: true

rollout:
  group_name: "RolloutGroup"
  backend: "huggingface"
  enable_offload: True
  pipeline_stage_num: 1
  model:
    model_path: ${actor.model.model_path}
    precision: ${actor.model.precision}

actor:
  group_name: "ActorGroup"
  training_backend: "fsdp"
  micro_batch_size: 32
  global_batch_size: 1024
  seed: 1234
  enable_offload: True

  # Override the default values in model/openpi
  model:
    model_path: "/mnt/nvme1/chenquan/RoboTwin/policy/pi05/checkpoints/pi05_base_pytorch" #"/path/to/model/RLinf-Pi0-SFT"
    num_action_chunks: 50 # interface for the env
    action_dim: 14
    use_proprio: True
    add_value_head: True
    num_steps: 5
    openpi:
      config_name: "pi0_aloha_robotwin"
      num_images_in_input: 3
      train_expert_only: True
      detach_critic_input: True

  optim:
    lr: 2.5e-5
    value_lr: 1.55e-4
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.95
    adam_eps: 1.0e-08
    weight_decay: 1e-10
    clip_grad: 1.0
    total_training_steps: 30000
    lr_warmup_steps: 1000
    lr_scheduler: "cosine"
    num_cycles: 0.5
    min_lr: 2.5e-6

  # Override the default values in training_backend/fsdp
  fsdp_config:
    strategy: "fsdp"
    gradient_checkpointing: True
    mixed_precision:
      param_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      reduce_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      buffer_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}

reward:
  use_reward_model: False

critic:
  use_critic_model: False

result.title: feat(openpi_rlinf): make model dtype configurable
result.body:
### Description
- `rlinf/models/embodiment/openpi_rlinf/__init__.py`: build the Pi0Config `dtype` from `cfg.precision` (default `bfloat16`) instead of hardcoding `"bfloat16"`, so the model load dtype follows the configured precision.
- `rlinf/models/embodiment/openpi_rlinf/pi0_model/utils.py`: extend `_str_to_dtype` with `float`/`fp32`/`bf16`/`fp16` aliases so common precision strings resolve without extra normalization.

### Motivation and Context
The vendored `openpi_rlinf` path hardcoded `dtype="bfloat16"` when constructing `Pi0Config`, which prevented loading/evaluating at other precisions (e.g. an fp32 master). `_str_to_dtype` also only recognized the long forms (`float32`/`bfloat16`/`float16`), so strings like `fp32`/`bf16` raised `KeyError`. This makes the dtype selection consistent with the rest of the stack (`torch_dtype_from_precision` / `normalize_dtype` already accept these aliases).

### How has this been tested?
- `from rlinf.models.embodiment.openpi_rlinf.pi0_model.pi0_config import Pi0Config` + `load_base_safetensors` strict-loads the converted Pi0.5 checkpoints (667 keys, 3.35B params) for both RoboTwin `adjust_bottle` and LIBERO `spatial`.
- `build_openpi_transforms(..., "pi05_libero"/"pi05_aloha_robotwin", ...)` resolves norm_stats from the converted checkpoint directories.
- No existing call site regresses: the default path (`precision` unset/`bfloat16`) is unchanged.

result.title: feat(embodied): add LingBot-VA RoboTwin evaluation support
result.body:
### Description

This PR adds official LingBot-VA support for RoboTwin evaluation in RLinf.

The main changes include:
- registering `lingbotva` as an embodied model in RLinf
- adding LingBot-VA rollout/evaluation integration on RoboTwin
- adding RoboTwin `ee` action support required by the official LingBot-VA inference workflow
- adding LingBot-VA install and asset download support
- adding LingBot-VA support to the shared RoboTwin Docker image
- adding embodied e2e and install workflow coverage for LingBot-VA on RoboTwin
- adding English and Chinese documentation pages for LingBot-VA evaluation

Current scope of this PR:
- RoboTwin evaluation only
- official LingBot-VA checkpoint inference only
- single-session evaluation per rollout worker
- `batch_size == 1`

This PR does **not** add SFT support for LingBot-VA yet.

### Motivation and Context

This change is required to integrate the official LingBot-VA RoboTwin checkpoint into RLinf, so that it can be loaded and evaluated inside RLinf's RoboTwin pipeline rather than only through the standalone upstream evaluation scripts.

The integration keeps the key model-side evaluation semantics required by LingBot-VA, including:
- 16D end-effector actions
- `add_init_pose`
- key-frame based chunk updates
- `compute_kv_cache` between chunks

At the same time, the implementation follows RLinf's embodied model conventions for config, install, Docker, e2e, and documentation.

### How has this been tested?

Static checks:
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed
- Python syntax checks passed for the LingBot-VA integration files via `py_compile`
- shell syntax checks passed for:
  - `requirements/install.sh`
  - `requirements/embodied/download_assets.sh`
  - `tests/e2e_tests/embodied/run_eval.sh`
- YAML parsing checks passed for:
  - `install.yml`
  - `embodied-e2e-tests.yml`
  - LingBot-VA example configs
  - LingBot-VA embodied e2e config

Local/runtime validation:
- `bash requirements/install.sh embodied --model lingbotva --env robotwin`
- `bash requirements/embodied/download_assets.sh --assets lingbotva`
- RoboTwin evaluation smoke tests:
  - `robotwin_click_bell_eval_lingbotva`: `eval/success_once = 1.0`
  - `robotwin_place_empty_cup_eval_lingbotva`: `eval/success_once = 1.0`

Notes on metrics:
- RLinf evaluation metrics are reported in RLinf's rollout aggregation format
- LingBot-VA is currently wired as RoboTwin evaluation only
- the validated configs keep `total_num_envs: 1`, `planner_backend: curobo`, `action_type: ee`, `action_dim: 16`, and `ignore_terminations: false`

### Additional information (optional, e.g., figures and logs):

Notes:
- This PR focuses on LingBot-VA RoboTwin evaluation support only.
- LingBot-VA SFT support is intentionally left for follow-up work.
- The install workflow step for LingBot-VA is guarded by `nvcc` availability, because the RoboTwin install path depends on CUDA toolchain support.

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update (Document-only update)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

### Configuration YAML file

defaults:
  - env/robotwin_place_empty_cup@env.train
  - env/robotwin_place_empty_cup@env.eval
  - model/openvla_oft@actor.model
  - training_backend/fsdp@actor.fsdp_config
  - override hydra/job_logging: stdout

hydra:
  run:
    dir: .
  output_subdir: null
  searchpath:
    - file://${oc.env:EMBODIED_PATH}/config/
    
cluster:
  num_nodes: 1
  component_placement:
    actor, env, rollout: 0-7

runner:
  task_type: embodied
  logger:
    log_path: "../results"
    project_name: rlinf
    experiment_name: "robotwin_grpo_openvlaoft"
    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 1000
  max_steps: -1

  only_eval: False
  val_check_interval: 20
  save_interval: 20

  resume_dir: null # Optional: path to a saved checkpoint directory, such as 'checkpoints/global_step_10'. If not None, it will be used to resume training.
  ckpt_path: null  # Optional: path to a .pt checkpoint. If not None, it will be loaded after the model is instantiated (for evaluation).

algorithm:
  normalize_advantages: True
  kl_penalty: kl  # how to estimate kl divergence: kl or kl_penalty
  group_size: 8

  rollout_epoch: 8
  eval_rollout_epoch: 1 # set eval_rollout_epoch > 0 when enable runner.only_eval or runner.val_check_interval > 0

  reward_type: action_level
  logprob_type: token_level
  entropy_type: token_level

  adv_type: grpo
  loss_type: actor
  loss_agg_func: "token-mean"
  kl_beta: 0.0
  entropy_bonus: 0
  clip_ratio_high: 0.28
  clip_ratio_low: 0.2
  clip_ratio_c: 3.0
  value_clip: 0.2
  huber_delta: 10.0

  gamma: 1.0
  gae_lambda: 0.95

  reward_coef: 5.0
  filter_rewards: True
  rewards_lower_bound: 0.5
  rewards_upper_bound: 4.5

  # params for rollout
  sampling_params:
    do_sample: True
    temperature_train: 1.6
    temperature_eval: -1 # -1 means do_sample=False during evaluation
    top_k: -1
    top_p: 1.0
    repetition_penalty: 1.0

  # length argument for autoregressive sampling
  # max length means max amount of tokens to generate
  length_params:
    max_new_token: null
    max_length: 512
    min_length: 1

env:
  group_name: "EnvGroup"
  enable_offload: True

  # Override the default values in env/robotwin_place_empty_cup
  train:
    total_num_envs: 128
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_episode_steps: 200
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 200
    group_size: ${algorithm.group_size}
    assets_path: "/robot/bionic-control-data/cr-disk/vlarl/RoboTwin/"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/train_seeds.json

  eval:
    total_num_envs: 128
    auto_reset: True
    ignore_terminations: True
    max_episode_steps: 200
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 200
    group_size: 1
    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: True
    is_eval: True
    assets_path: "/robot/bionic-control-data/cr-disk/vlarl/RoboTwin/"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/eval_seeds.json
    video_cfg:
      save_video: True
      video_base_dir: ${runner.logger.log_path}/video/eval

rollout:
  group_name: "RolloutGroup"
  backend: "huggingface"
  enable_offload: True
  pipeline_stage_num: 1
  model:
    model_type: "openvla_oft"
    model_path: ${actor.model.model_path}
    precision: ${actor.model.precision}

actor:
  group_name: "ActorGroup"
  training_backend: "fsdp"
  micro_batch_size: 32
  global_batch_size: 1024
  seed: 1234
  enable_offload: True

  # Override the default values in model/openvla_oft
  model:
    model_path: "/robot/bionic-control-data/cr-disk/vlarl/RLinf/RLinf-OpenVLAOFT-RoboTwin-SFT-place_empty_cup"
    implement_version: "offical"
    model_type: "openvla_oft"
    value_type: ${algorithm.reward_type}  # 'action' or 'token'
    action_dim: 14
    use_proprio: True
    proprio_dim: 14
    use_film: False

    num_action_chunks: 25
    unnorm_key: place_empty_cup_1k
    center_crop: True

    is_lora: True
    max_prompt_length: 512

  optim:
    lr: 1.0e-4
    value_lr: 1.0e-5
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.999
    adam_eps: 1.0e-05
    weight_decay: 0.01
    clip_grad: 1.0

  # Override the default values in training_backend/fsdp
  fsdp_config:
    strategy: "fsdp"
    gradient_checkpointing: True
    mixed_precision:
      param_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      reduce_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      buffer_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}

reward:
  use_reward_model: False

critic:
  use_critic_model: False

result.title: [Feature]: Implement a shared-GPU batched VectorEnv for RobotWin with SAPIEN
result.body:
### Feature description

RobotWin currently scales environment throughput by running many independent sub-environments, each with its own scene, simulation loop, rendering path, and Python-side orchestration, which introduces substantial per-environment overhead at higher parallelism. SAPIEN already provides the primitives needed for a true shared-GPU batched vector environment, including PhysxGpuSystem, scene offsets for multiple environments inside one GPU simulation, CUDA articulation state and target buffers, and grouped camera rendering. This makes it feasible to build a RobotWin VectorEnv backend where multiple environment slots share one GPU physics and rendering runtime while preserving the existing rollout interface, reducing simulation and observation overhead and establishing a general foundation for batched execution across RobotWin tasks.

result.title: RoboTwin GRPO rollout too slow; possible weak GPU parallelization of environments
result.body:
### Problem description

We are reproducing OpenVLA-OFT reinforcement learning (GRPO) on RoboTwin. Only the “total_num_envs: 128 -> 32” and "group_size: 8 -> 4" in the default config. With this change, the rollout phase is very slow（30:15 for 1 training step, 8 rollout_epochs）. We suspect that parallel robotwin environment execution on 8*H200 is not scaling well in my conda environment, so rollout becomes the bottleneck. We are looking for the intended way to speed up so that rollout time stays acceptable.

result.title: Reproduction issue: OpenVLA-OFT RoboTwin PPO
result.body:
### Problem description

We are trying to reproduce OpenVLA-OFT reinforcement learning (PPO) training on the RoboTwin (place_empty_cup) setup in RLinf. We only modified the default configuration for environment count (e.g. total_num_envs and/or group_size) and GPU ranks for actor, env, rollout.  With these changes, training behavior or results are not satisfied. We are looking for the correct way to reproduce the training result.

### Configuration YAML file

env:
  train:
    env_type: robotwin
    total_num_envs: 8
    auto_reset: false
    ignore_terminations: false
    reward_coef: 1.0
    use_custom_reward: true
    use_rel_reward: true
    seed: 0
    group_size: 1
    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: false
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 200
    max_episode_steps: 200

result.title: [Troubleshoot]: RL training with pi0.5 and GRPO in RoboTwin is unstable.
result.body:
### Problem description

Using pi0.5 as the VLA, with absolute joint positions as the action space and the action chunk set to 16, GRPO-based RL training in the place_cans_plastic scenario is unstable.

### Configuration YAML file

YAML config file:

You can also paste the full config here.
```
defaults:
  - env/robotwin_place_cans_plasticbox@env.train
  - env/robotwin_place_cans_plasticbox@env.eval
  - model/pi0_5@actor.model
  - training_backend/fsdp@actor.fsdp_config
  - weight_syncer/patch_syncer@weight_syncer
  - override hydra/job_logging: stdout

hydra:
  run:
    dir: .
  output_subdir: null
  searchpath:
    - file://${oc.env:EMBODIED_PATH}/config/

cluster:
  num_nodes: 1
  component_placement:
    actor, env, rollout: 0,1,3,4,5,6

runner:
  task_type: embodied
  logger:
    log_path: "../results"
    project_name: rlinf
    experiment_name: "robotwin_grpo_openpi_pi05"
    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 1000
  max_steps: -1

  only_eval: False
  val_check_interval: -1
  save_interval: 10

  resume_dir: null # Optional: path to a saved checkpoint directory, such as 'checkpoints/global_step_10'. If not None, it will be used to resume training.
  ckpt_path: null  # Optional: path to a .pt checkpoint. If not None, it will be loaded after the model is instantiated (for evaluation).

algorithm:
  normalize_advantages: True
  kl_penalty: kl  # how to estimate kl divergence: kl or kl_penalty
  group_size: 8
  reward_coef: 1.0

  rollout_epoch: 4
  eval_rollout_epoch: 1 # set eval_rollout_epoch > 0 when enable runner.only_eval or runner.val_check_interval > 0

  reward_type: chunk_level
  logprob_type: chunk_level
  entropy_type: token_level

  update_epoch: 5
  adv_type: grpo
  loss_type: actor
  loss_agg_func: "token-mean" 
  kl_beta: 0.0
  entropy_bonus: 0
  clip_ratio_high: 0.2
  clip_ratio_low: 0.2
  clip_ratio_c: 3.0
  value_clip: 0.2
  huber_delta: 10.0

  gamma: 0.99
  gae_lambda: 0.95

  filter_rewards: True
  rewards_lower_bound: 0.1
  rewards_upper_bound: 0.9
  # params for generation
  sampling_params:
    do_sample: True
    temperature_train: 1.0
    temperature_eval: 0.6
    top_k: 50
    top_p: 1.0
    repetition_penalty: 1.0
    add_BOS: False

  # length argument for autoregressive sampling
  # max length means max amount of tokens to generate
  length_params:
    max_new_token: null
    max_length: 1024
    min_length: 1

env:
  group_name: "EnvGroup"
  enable_offload: True
  # Override the default values in env/robotwin_place_cans_plasticbox
  train:
    total_num_envs: 240
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_episode_steps: 320
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 320
    group_size: ${algorithm.group_size}
    assets_path: "/data/zsq/RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/train_seeds.json
    center_crop: False
    task_config:
      embodiment: [aloha-agilex]
      camera:
        collect_wrist_camera: true
      domain_randomization:
        random_background: false
        cluttered_table: false
        clean_background_rate: 1
        random_head_camera_dis: 0
        random_table_height: 0
        random_light: false
        crazy_random_light_rate: 0
  eval:
    total_num_envs: 240
    auto_reset: True
    ignore_terminations: True
    max_episode_steps: 320
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 320
    group_size: 1
    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: True
    is_eval: True
    assets_path: "/data/zsq/RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/eval_seeds.json
    video_cfg:
      save_video: True
      video_base_dir: ${runner.logger.log_path}/video/eval
    center_crop: False
    task_config:
      embodiment: [aloha-agilex]
      camera:
        collect_wrist_camera: true
      domain_randomization:
        random_background: false
        cluttered_table: false
        clean_background_rate: 1
        random_head_camera_dis: 0
        random_table_height: 0
        random_light: false
        crazy_random_light_rate: 0

rollout:
  group_name: "RolloutGroup"
  backend: "huggingface"
  recompute_logprobs: False
  enable_offload: True
  pipeline_stage_num: 1
  model:
    model_path: ${actor.model.model_path}
    precision: ${actor.model.precision}

actor:
  group_name: "ActorGroup"
  training_backend: "fsdp"
  micro_batch_size: 40
  global_batch_size: 960 # 1024
  seed: 42
  enable_offload: False

  # Override the default values in model/openpi_pi05
  model:
    model_path: "/data/zsq/pi05_ckpt/robotwin_place_cans_plastic/20000_torch"
    num_action_chunks: 16 # interface for the env
    action_dim: 14
    # add_value_head: True
    num_steps: 5
    use_proprio: True
    openpi_data:
      adapt_to_pi: False
      extra_delta_transform: False
    openpi:
      config_name: pi05_robotwin
      num_images_in_input: 3
      action_chunk: ${actor.model.num_action_chunks}
      action_env_dim: ${actor.model.action_dim}
      num_steps: ${actor.model.num_steps}
      noise_method: "flow_sde"
      noise_level: 0.3
      # value_after_vlm: True
      # detach_critic_input: True

  optim:
    lr: 5.0e-06
    value_lr: 1.0e-04
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.95
    adam_eps: 1.0e-08
    weight_decay: 0.01
    clip_grad: 1.0
    critic_warmup_steps: 0

  # Override the default values in training_backend/fsdp
  fsdp_config:
    strategy: "fsdp"
    gradient_checkpointing: False # for openpi, gradient checkpointing is not supported, please do not change this value
    mixed_precision:
      param_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      reduce_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      buffer_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}

reward:
  use_reward_model: False

critic:
  use_critic_model: False
```

result.body:
### Affected component

Could you provide a complete user guide for the robotwin OpenPI project (current documentation tends to focus on openvla-oft)? I've noticed many people in the comments section reporting bugs in the robotwin OpenPI project.

### Bug description

(EmbodiedFSDPActor pid=1406394) [INFO 08:50:22 ActorGroup-Rank-0][fsdp_model_manager.py:107] [FSDP] AMP is disabled.

### Configuration YAML file

defaults:
  - env/robotwin_place_empty_cup@env.train
  - env/robotwin_place_empty_cup@env.eval
  - model/pi0@actor.model
  - training_backend/fsdp@actor.fsdp_config
  - override hydra/job_logging: stdout

hydra:
  run:
    dir: .
  output_subdir: null
  searchpath:
    - file://${oc.env:EMBODIED_PATH}/config/
    
cluster:
  num_nodes: 1
  component_placement:
    actor, env, rollout: 0-3

runner:
  task_type: embodied
  logger:
    log_path: "../results"
    project_name: rlinf
    experiment_name: "robotwin_grpo_openpi"
    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 1000
  max_steps: -1

  only_eval: True
  val_check_interval: 20
  save_interval: 20

  resume_dir: null # Optional: path to a saved checkpoint directory, such as 'checkpoints/global_step_10'. If not None, it will be used to resume training.
  ckpt_path: null  # Optional: path to a .pt checkpoint. If not None, it will be loaded after the model is instantiated (for evaluation).

algorithm:
  normalize_advantages: True
  kl_penalty: kl  # how to estimate kl divergence: kl or kl_penalty
  group_size: 8

  rollout_epoch: 8
  eval_rollout_epoch: 1 # set eval_rollout_epoch > 0 when enable runner.only_eval or runner.val_check_interval > 0

  reward_type: action_level
  logprob_type: token_level
  entropy_type: token_level

  adv_type: grpo
  loss_type: actor
  loss_agg_func: "token-mean"
  kl_beta: 0.0
  entropy_bonus: 0
  clip_ratio_high: 0.28
  clip_ratio_low: 0.2
  clip_ratio_c: 3.0
  value_clip: 0.2
  huber_delta: 10.0

  gamma: 1.0
  gae_lambda: 0.95

  reward_coef: 5.0
  filter_rewards: True
  rewards_lower_bound: 0.5
  rewards_upper_bound: 4.5

  # params for rollout
  sampling_params:
    do_sample: True
    temperature_train: 1.6
    temperature_eval: -1 # -1 means do_sample=False during evaluation
    top_k: -1
    top_p: 1.0
    repetition_penalty: 1.0

  # length argument for autoregressive sampling
  # max length means max amount of tokens to generate
  length_params:
    max_new_token: null
    max_length: 512
    min_length: 1

env:
  group_name: "EnvGroup"
  enable_offload: True

  # Override the default values in env/robotwin_place_empty_cup
  train:
    total_num_envs: 128
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_episode_steps: 200
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 200
    group_size: ${algorithm.group_size}
    assets_path: "/mnt/nvme1/chenquan/RLinf/RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/train_seeds.json
    center_crop: False
    task_config:
      embodiment: [aloha-agilex]
      camera:
        collect_wrist_camera: true
  eval:
    total_num_envs: 128
    auto_reset: True
    ignore_terminations: True
    max_episode_steps: 200
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 200
    group_size: 1
    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: True
    is_eval: True
    assets_path: "/mnt/nvme1/chenquan/RLinf/RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/eval_seeds.json
    center_crop: False
    video_cfg:
      save_video: True
      video_base_dir: ${runner.logger.log_path}/video/eval
    task_config:
      embodiment: [aloha-agilex]
      camera:
        collect_wrist_camera: true

rollout:
  group_name: "RolloutGroup"
  backend: "huggingface"
  enable_offload: True
  pipeline_stage_num: 1
  model:
    model_path: ${actor.model.model_path}
    precision: ${actor.model.precision}

actor:
  group_name: "ActorGroup"
  training_backend: "fsdp"
  micro_batch_size: 32
  global_batch_size: 1024
  seed: 1234
  enable_offload: True

  # Override the default values in model/openpi
  model:
    model_path: "/mnt/nvme1/chenquan/RoboTwin/policy/pi05/checkpoints/pi05_base_pytorch" #"/path/to/model/RLinf-Pi0-SFT"
    num_action_chunks: 50 # interface for the env
    action_dim: 14
    use_proprio: True
    add_value_head: True
    num_steps: 5
    openpi:
      config_name: "pi0_aloha_robotwin"
      num_images_in_input: 3
      train_expert_only: True
      detach_critic_input: True

  optim:
    lr: 2.5e-5
    value_lr: 1.55e-4
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.95
    adam_eps: 1.0e-08
    weight_decay: 1e-10
    clip_grad: 1.0
    total_training_steps: 30000
    lr_warmup_steps: 1000
    lr_scheduler: "cosine"
    num_cycles: 0.5
    min_lr: 2.5e-6

  # Override the default values in training_backend/fsdp
  fsdp_config:
    strategy: "fsdp"
    gradient_checkpointing: True
    mixed_precision:
      param_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      reduce_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      buffer_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}

reward:
  use_reward_model: False

critic:
  use_critic_model: False


### Log file

You can find the log file in `logs/` folder or the $output_dir/$experiment_name folder (defined in the yaml config) if you are using our example scripts.

Log file:

If you cannot find the log, please provide the full log messages here.
```
<paste log here>
```

result.title: [Troubleshoot]: CUDA Out of Memory error during training
result.body:
### Problem description

hi @chenkang455, I noticed that you have answered #537  before, and now I am facing the same problem. I used 8 40G A100 and made the following modifications to the parameters according to your suggestions, but OOM still occurs at random positions during the training process. Can you give me some advice?
```
rollout_epoch: 8->4->2
total_num_envs: 128->64->32
micro_batch_size: 32->8->4
global_batch_size: 1024->256
all enable_offload: True
```
I noticed that OOM occurred during the training process for above all parameter configurations. For example, 20 steps, 24 steps..... I wonder if there are some values that were not released during the training process, leading to accumulation? Thank you!

    project_name: rlinf

    logger_backends: ["tensorboard"] # wandb, swanlab

  max_epochs: 1000
  max_steps: -1

  only_eval: False
  val_check_interval: 20
  save_interval: 100

  resume_dir: null # Optional: path to a saved checkpoint directory, such as 'checkpoints/global_step_10'. If not None, it will be used to resume training.
  ckpt_path: null  # Optional: path to a .pt checkpoint. If not None, it will be loaded after the model is instantiated (for evaluation).

algorithm:
  normalize_advantages: True
  kl_penalty: kl  # how to estimate kl divergence: kl or kl_penalty
  group_size: 8
  update_epoch: 2
  rollout_epoch: 4
  eval_rollout_epoch: 1 # set eval_rollout_epoch > 0 when enable runner.only_eval or runner.val_check_interval > 0

  reward_type: action_level
  logprob_type: token_level
  entropy_type: token_level

  adv_type: grpo
  loss_type: actor
  loss_agg_func: "token-mean"
  kl_beta: 0.05
  entropy_bonus: 0.05
  clip_ratio_high: 0.28
  clip_ratio_low: 0.2
  clip_ratio_c: 3.0
  value_clip: 0.2
  huber_delta: 10.0

  gamma: 1.0
  gae_lambda: 0.95

  reward_coef: 5.0
  filter_rewards: False
  rewards_lower_bound: 0.5
  rewards_upper_bound: 4.5

 # params for rollout
  sampling_params:
    do_sample: True
    temperature_train: 1.6
    temperature_eval: -1 # -1 means do_sample=False during evaluation
    top_k: -1
    top_p: 1.0
    repetition_penalty: 1.0

  # length argument for autoregressive sampling
  # max length means max amount of tokens to generate
  length_params:
    max_new_token: null
    max_length: 1024
    min_length: 1

env:
  group_name: "EnvGroup"

  # Override the default values in env/robotwin_click_bell
  train:
    total_num_envs: 32
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    use_custom_reward: False
    use_rel_reward: True
    video_cfg:
      save_video: True
    max_episode_steps: 400
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 400
    group_size: ${algorithm.group_size}
    assets_path: "RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/train_seeds.json
    enable_offload: True

  eval:
    total_num_envs: 32
    use_custom_reward: False
    use_rel_reward: True
    auto_reset: True
    ignore_terminations: True
    max_episode_steps: 400
    reward_coef: ${algorithm.reward_coef}
    max_steps_per_rollout_epoch: 400
    group_size: 1
    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: True 
    is_eval: True
    assets_path: "RoboTwin"
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/eval_seeds.json
    video_cfg:
      save_video: True
      video_base_dir: ${runner.logger.log_path}/video/eval
    enable_offload: True

rollout:
  group_name: "RolloutGroup"
  backend: "huggingface"
  enable_offload: True
  pipeline_stage_num: 1
  model:
    model_type: "lingbotvla"
    model_path: ${actor.model.model_path}
    tokenizer_path: ${actor.model.tokenizer_path}
    precision: ${actor.model.precision}

actor:
  group_name: "ActorGroup"
  training_backend: "fsdp"
  micro_batch_size: 8
  global_batch_size: 256
  seed: 1234
  enable_offload: True

  # Override the default values in model/lingbotvla
  model:
    model_path: "lingbot-vla-4b-posttrain-robotwin"
    tokenizer_path: "Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct"
    model_type: "lingbotvla"
    lingbotvla:
      config_path: "lingbot-vla-4b-posttrain-robotwin"
    value_type: ${algorithm.reward_type}  # 'action' or 'token'
    action_dim: 14
    use_proprio: True
    proprio_dim: 14

    num_action_chunks: 50
    is_lora: False
    max_prompt_length: 512

    num_steps: 10              
    noise_method: "flow_sde"   
    noise_level: 0.7           
    joint_logprob: False       
    action_env_dim: 14         
    add_value_head: False
    safe_get_logprob: False

  optim:
    lr: 1.0e-5
    value_lr: 1.0e-5
    adam_beta1: 0.9
    adam_beta2: 0.999
    adam_eps: 1.0e-05
    weight_decay: 0.01
    clip_grad: 1.0

  # Override the default values in training_backend/fsdp
  fsdp_config:
    strategy: "fsdp"
    gradient_checkpointing: True
    mixed_precision:
      param_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      reduce_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}
      buffer_dtype: ${actor.model.precision}

reward:
  use_reward_model: False

critic:
  use_critic_model: False

result.title: feat(robotwin): expose native environment capabilities
result.body:
### Description

Expose stable RoboTwin native environment capabilities for downstream runtimes while preserving the existing training paths.

- Execute native RoboTwin action chunks with qpos14 or EEF16 actions.
- Expose robot state, native episode status, and arm path planning.
- Expose raw RGB/depth rendering, camera calibration metadata, and task language.
- Support exact-seed reset while synchronizing RLinf training bookkeeping.

### Motivation and Context

Downstream integrations should use stable RLinf environment APIs instead of accessing private RoboTwin task, robot, camera, or planner objects directly.

RLinf remains the owner of the native RoboTwin environment and simulator-specific capabilities. Higher-level Agent observation assembly, primitive composition, and episode lifecycle handling are owned by downstream runtimes such as RPent.

### How has this been tested?

- Ruff, format, compilation, and deterministic API contract checks.
- RoboTwin common reset/step/chunk execution and exact-seed reset.
- Raw RGB/depth rendering and camera metadata checks.
- Native qpos14 and EEF16 action execution, robot-state access, episode status, and arm planning.
- End-to-end RPent integration smoke with LingBot-VLA and clean process shutdown.
- Latest source-overlay integration run completed 25 cases across 5 RoboTwin tasks and verified task-specific native action budgets.

### Additional information

The existing training `reset()`, `step()`, and `chunk_step()` paths are unchanged.

Episode-level terminal tracking and higher-level Agent lifecycle handling are intentionally kept outside RLinf.

result.title: fix(config): increase clear_cache_freq from 1 to 8 for robotwin tasks
result.body: ### Description Increase clear_cache_freq from 1 to 8 for RoboTwin tasks. By decreasing the cache clearing frequency and reducing cache cleanup overhead, we can reduce the environment bootstrap and reset time per instance from ~400s to ~70s. Considering that a typical configuration uses 8 rollout epochs (requiring 8 bootstraps), reducing the overall bootstrap time for RoboTwin environments from ~3200s to ~560s significantly cuts step time (from ~1h down to ~30min) and improves overall training efficiency. ### Motivation and Context In some RoboTwin training experiments, the environment bootstrap time took longer than the actual rollout interaction and execution time, which is unacceptable and requires optimization. ### How has this been tested? An experiment on robotwin_adjust_bottle_ppo_openpi shows after increase clear cache freq，bootstrap time reduced from ~370s to ~70s ### Additional information (optional, e.g., figures and logs): It worth noting that increasing clear cache freq could cause unfavorable impact on GPU memory usage. But since robotwin asset are mostly fixed for each experiment settings, I don't foresee increase clear_cache_freq from 1 to 8 could cause dramatic memory increase that casuse OOM. Further experiment has to be conducted to prove this point. Update: A further comprehensive test on robotwin_adjust_bottle_ppo_openpi has been conducted, with a config 256 envs 8 rollout epoch (RLinf default cfg) ang 2 steps. No signs of memory pressure and no OOM occurred. (In fig red bars within bottem part denote env bootstrap ~40s, green blocks denote env interact/obs action). ### Types of changes - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Documentation update (Document-only update) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) ### Checklist: - [x] My code follows the code style of this project. - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. - [ ] I have added tests to cover my changes. - [ ] All new and existing tests passed.

result.title: [Usage]: [Bug] Zero success rate with beat_block_hammer OpenVLA-OFT (RLinf-GRPO) checkpoint on RoboTwin 2.0
result.body: ### Problem description Hi team, thanks for this great work. I am currently evaluating the benchmarks using the official checkpoints provided in the documentation. However, I encountered an issue with the beat_block_hammer task. **Issue Description:** When testing with the OpenVLA-OFT (RLinf-GRPO) weights for beat_block_hammer, I consistently get a 0% success rate. **Context & Observations:** I have verified my environment and evaluation pipeline by testing other checkpoint groups (6 other sets), and **their results are generally consistent with the reported numbers.** This suggests the issue might be specific to this particular weight file. **Question:** Could you please double-check if the correct weights were uploaded to Hugging Face for this specific task? result.title: feat(openpi): add jax-aligned pytorch SFT for pi0
result.body: ### Description Add JAX-aligned PyTorch OpenPI (`openpi_pytorch`) support in RLinf, with maintained SFT and evaluation workflows for: - Pi0 on RoboTwin - Pi0.5 on BEHAVIOR-1K For RoboTwin Pi0, this PR provides: - SFT using the official OpenPI/LeRobot dataloader. - Explicit YAML configuration for task-specific normalization statistics. - Conversion from RLinf SFT `full_weights.pt` checkpoints to the new HF-style PyTorch checkpoint format. - An `adjust_bottle` evaluation recipe using the converted checkpoint. The implementation keeps the SFT worker generic: RoboTwin-specific paths and normalization statistics are declared in YAML rather than hard-coded in training logic. English and Chinese documentation are included, and the SFT gallery links to the OpenPI PyTorch guide. ### Motivation and Context Provide reproducible PyTorch OpenPI SFT entry points that follow the JAX reference behavior while fitting RLinf's training, checkpoint, and evaluation workflows. ### How has this been tested? - pi0 robotwin on adjust_bottle task ,final eval results for 2w step ckpt is 90.625% - Ran `tests/unit_tests/test_openpi_sft2rlinf_pytorch.py` (`4 passed`). - On the training server, created an official RoboTwin OpenPI dataloader batch and verified that task-specific `adjust_bottle` normalization statistics were loaded. - Converted a real RoboTwin Pi0 SFT step-30k `full_weights.pt` checkpoint and strictly loaded the resulting HF checkpoint through the `openpi_pytorch` eval model. - Parsed the modified RST files with Docutils. A full Sphinx HTML build was not run locally because `myst_parser` and `pydata_sphinx_theme` are unavailable. A full RoboTwin simulator evaluation is also outside this PR's automated test coverage. ### Additional information The maintained SFT matrix is: - Pi0 + RoboTwin - Pi0.5 + BEHAVIOR-1K Pi0 + BEHAVIOR-1K does not currently have a maintained SFT recipe. ### Types of changes - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [x] Documentation update - [ ] Breaking change ### Checklist - [x] My code follows the code style of this project. - [x] My change requires documentation updates. - [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly. - [x] I have added or updated relevant tests. - [ ] All new and existing CI tests passed.

result.title: [Feature]: Blackwell (sm_100/sm_120) Docker Image Support for VLA Post-training
result.body:
### Feature description

## Blackwell (sm_100/sm_120) Docker Image Support

### Summary

The official RLinf Docker images are based on CUDA 12.4, which does not support NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (B200/B100 sm_100, RTX PRO 5000/5090/6000 sm_120). I've built and verified a community Docker image that enables RLinf embodied training on Blackwell hardware.

- **Docker Hub**: [`chenchaox72877/rlinf:0.2-maniskill_libero-blackwell`](https://hub.docker.com/r/chenchaox72877/rlinf/tags)
- **Dockerfile**: [`docker/Dockerfile.blackwell`](https://github.com/chenchaoxu7575/RLinf/blob/feat/blackwell-docker/docker/Dockerfile.blackwell)

### What's different from the official `rlinf/rlinf:agentic-rlinf0.2-maniskill_libero`

| | Official | Blackwell |
|--|---------|-----------|
| Base image | `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1` | `nvidia/cuda:12.8.1` |
| torch | auto-resolved (cu124) | `2.7.1+cu128` (exact wheel URL) |
| NCCL | bundled 2.21~2.26 | upgraded to 2.28.9 |
| flash-attn | precompiled wheel (sm_90) | cross-compiled (sm_90 + sm_100 + sm_120) |
| nccl-rdma-sharp-plugins | not included | compiled against NCCL 2.28.9 |
| nsight-systems | not included | 2025.3.1 |
| Included venvs | 6 (openvla, openvla-oft, openpi, gr00t, dexbotic, starvla) | 2 (openpi, openvla), others not tested |

### Why these changes are needed

1. **CUDA 12.8 base**: Blackwell GPUs require CUDA 12.8+ runtime for sm_100/sm_120 kernel support.

2. **Exact torch cu128 wheels**: `UV_TORCH_BACKEND=auto` fails to detect the CUDA version during Docker build, falling back to cu124. We pin exact wheel URLs (`torch-2.7.1+cu128-cp311-cp311-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl`) to ensure correct CUDA backend.

3. **NCCL 2.28.9**: NCCL 2.26.2 bundled with torch 2.7.1 has a known Blackwell bug — `ncclDevKernel_SendRecv` performs out-of-bounds writes during cross-node communication, causing `CUDA error: illegal memory access`. References: #170003 (pytorch/pytorch), #152780 (pytorch/pytorch).

4. **flash-attn cross-compilation**: flash-attn is functionally required on Blackwell. Without it, transformers falls back to SDPA attention, which triggers `illegal memory access` during `load_state_dict`. The precompiled wheel only contains sm_90 kernels, so we cross-compile with `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="9.0;10.0;12.0"`.

5. **nccl-rdma-sharp-plugins**: Required for InfiniBand RDMA transport. Must be compiled against the matching NCCL version (2.28.9).

### Verified hardware

| GPU | Driver | Status |
|-----|--------|--------|
| RTX PRO 5000 (sm_120) | 580.95 / CUDA 13.0 | Verified |

### Verified experiments

- 2-node Pi0.5 SAC DSRL async training (1-rank per node, IB 400Gbps)
- Environment: openpi venv

### Related

- #565 added `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` Blackwell support in `install.sh` for the robotwin environment. This image extends Blackwell support to a full Docker image for the `maniskill_libero` embodied environment.
- #92 

### Usage

```bash
# Pull
docker pull chenchaox72877/rlinf:0.2-maniskill_libero-blackwell

# Or build from Dockerfile (build context = RLinf repo root)
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.blackwell -t rlinf-blackwell:latest .
```

### Additional context

_No response_

result.title: fix(embodiment): avoid DAgger bootstrap mask mismatch
result.body:
### Description

This PR fixes a DAgger rollout regression introduced after the RLT integration.

Before PR #1352, DAgger used `RolloutResult.save_flags` to mark expert-labeled chunks that should be saved and used for training. Later, when trajectories were built, those `save_flags` were mapped into `Trajectory.intervene_flags` only because the existing DAgger actor still consumes trajectories through `extract_intervene_traj(mode="all")`.

After the RLT changes, this DAgger save/train mask was routed through `RolloutResult.intervene_flags` instead. That mixed two different meanings in the same field:

- For RLT, `intervene_flags` means actual expert intervention/takeover.
- For DAgger, the flag is a save/train mask for expert-labeled data.

This PR restores the old DAgger data path by:
- Restoring `RolloutResult.save_flags` for DAgger expert-label save masks.
- Keeping `RolloutResult.intervene_flags` for actual intervention semantics.
- Passing `save_flags` through rollout result merge/split.
- Mapping `save_flags` back into final `Trajectory.intervene_flags` only for the legacy DAgger extraction path.
- Skipping final bootstrap `actions` and `forward_inputs` append for DAgger.

### Motivation and Context

`robotwin_adjust_bottle_dagger_openpi` can fail with:

```text
IndexError: The shape of the mask [5] at index 0 does not match the shape of the indexed tensor [4, 50] at index 0
```

The direct cause is a trajectory length mismatch. DAgger can produce a `trajectory.intervene_flags` mask with one more timestep than `trajectory.rewards`.

That extra mask row comes from the final bootstrap rollout result. The final bootstrap result is needed to compute bootstrap values/rewards, but it should not create another normal training action step for DAgger. Previously, it still appended `actions` and `forward_inputs`. Since `EmbodiedRolloutResult.append_step_result()` creates an `intervene_flags` row whenever `actions` exists, this added one extra mask row without a matching reward row.

The deeper issue is the flag semantic regression after RLT was added. DAgger's original `save_flags` path was collapsed into `intervene_flags`, while RLT also uses `intervene_flags` for real expert takeover. This made DAgger depend on a field whose meaning had changed.

This PR restores DAgger behavior close to the pre-PR #1352 implementation while preserving the RLT meaning of `intervene_flags`.

### How has this been tested?

RoboTwin and RLT can be trained as they should be and results is alright.

result.title: fix(robotwin): cover multi-worker seed partition
result.body:
## Summary

- Adds a lightweight regression test for the RoboTwin multi-worker success seed partition logic introduced in #1196.
- Extracts the partition logic into a small helper so the behavior can be tested without launching RoboTwin/SAPIEN or any GPU environment.
- Verifies that 128 eval episodes remain unique across 4/8/16 workers and several representative RoboTwin success-seed counts.

## Notes

This PR is intended as a follow-up to #1196 / #1175. It is currently based on #1196's fix commit, so the diff includes that change until #1196 is merged. After #1196 lands, this PR should reduce to the helper extraction plus regression test.

## Test

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$(pwd):$(pwd)/tests/unit_tests pytest tests/unit_tests/test_robotwin_seed_partition.py -q
ruff check rlinf/envs/robotwin/seed_utils.py rlinf/envs/robotwin/robotwin_env.py tests/unit_tests/test_robotwin_seed_partition.py
```

Local result: 7 passed; ruff passed when run inside the RoboTwin/OpenVLA-OFT environment used for local validation.

result.title: fix(embodied): update LingbotVLA RoboTwin SFT path
result.body: ### Description This PR updates the RLinf LingbotVLA RoboTwin integration to align with the upstream March RoboTwin SFT inference path from Robbyant/LingbotVLA. Main changes: - Align LingbotVLA model loading with the March `lingbot_robotwin_policy_rep.py` path. - Load `lingbotvla_cli.yaml` from `model_path` / `lingbotvla.config_path`. - Merge LingbotVLA model/train config with Qwen `AutoConfig`. - Use the upstream LingbotVLA processor builder. - Use the RoboTwin rep normalizer/statistics convention. - Apply the official RoboTwin state/action reorder rules. - Keep RLinf GRPO/PPO sampling, logprob, value, and training interfaces intact. - Add an `rl_trainable_scope` option and default LingbotVLA GRPO training to `action_expert` scope to reduce SFT drift. - Update LingbotVLA docs with the pinned RoboTwin SFT model download command and the success curve reference. ### Motivation and Context The current RLinf LingbotVLA path was based on the earlier February integration. The upstream LingbotVLA RoboTwin SFT release later moved to the March `lingbot_robotwin_policy_rep.py` inference path, which changes config loading, processor construction, normalization, and state/action ordering. Without this update, the official RoboTwin SFT checkpoint can show unexpectedly poor performance in RLinf on some RoboTwin tasks. Thanks to @fleetfootwork for pointing out that the upstream LingbotVLA RoboTwin SFT release had moved to the March `lingbot_robotwin_policy_rep.py` path, and for helping analyze and test the RLinf integration update. ### How has this been tested? Tested with: - Official RLinf checkout based on `44b4b50` - RoboTwin `RLinf_support` - LingbotVLA RoboTwin SFT checkpoint: - `robbyant/lingbot-vla-4b-posttrain-robotwin` - revision `3e0c7c476bde3daaac00f79f3741a292a299f60a` - Qwen tokenizer/config: - `Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` Checks run: - `git diff --check` - `pre-commit run --files ...` - `python -m py_compile rlinf/models/embodiment/lingbotvla/lingbotvla_action_model.py` - RoboTwin LingbotVLA evaluation and GRPO smoke/long-run checks Observed training curve: Observed evaluation comparison: click bell task： Additional result: Starting from the `click_bell` GRPO `global_step_45` checkpoint, I continued GRPO fine-tuning on the `place_shoe` task. The training `env/success_once` remains around `0.95`, and periodic evaluation reaches `eval/success_once = 0.9844` at step 59. ### Types of changes - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [x] Documentation update (Document-only update) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) ### Checklist - [x] My code follows the code style of this project. - [x] My change requires a change to the documentation. - [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly. - [x] I have added tests or validation notes to cover my changes. - [x] All new and existing applicable checks passed.

result.title: feat(embodiment): add dagger for robotwin
result.body: ### Description I added DAgger algorithm compatibility to the RoboTwin. ### Motivation and Context The RoboTwin environment requires the addition of the DAgger algorithm. ### How has this been tested? Following the [doc](https://rlinf.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/rst_source/examples/embodied/dagger.html) of current DAgger. Already tested the new DAgger for RoboTwin adjust_bottle task. Expert model: [RLinf-Pi0-RoboTwin-PPO-adjust_bottle](https://huggingface.co/RLinf/RLinf-Pi0-RoboTwin-PPO-adjust_bottle), which success rate is around 98%. Student model: [RLinf-Pi0-RoboTwin-SFT-adjust_bottle](https://huggingface.co/RLinf/RLinf-Pi0-RoboTwin-SFT-adjust_bottle), which success rate is around 75%. Sync Mode: Run `bash examples/embodiment/run_embodiment.sh robotwin_adjust_bottle_dagger_openpi` set `only_save_expert` as `False` (default setting, aligned with existing DAgger settings) Async Mode: Run `bash examples/embodiment/run_async.sh robotwin_adjust_bottle_dagger_openpi` set `only_save_expert` as `False` (default setting, aligned with existing DAgger settings) Async Mode: Run `bash examples/embodiment/run_async.sh robotwin_adjust_bottle_dagger_openpi` set `only_save_expert` as `True` ### Additional information (optional, e.g., figures and logs): The corresponding experimental results are shown in the previous column. The newly added content is relatively independent and should not interfere with other existing functions. ### Types of changes - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Documentation update (Document-only update) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) ### Checklist: - [x] My code follows the code style of this project. - [x] My change requires a change to the documentation. - [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly. - [x] I have added tests to cover my changes. - [x] All new and existing tests passed.

result.title: fix(robotwin): eliminate duplicate seeds across EnvWorkers
result.body:
## Summary

- Fixes #1175: RoboTwin evaluation workers were each independently shuffling the full `success_seeds` list with a per-worker seed (`base_seed + seed_offset`), then all drawing from index 0 of their differently-shuffled lists. This caused the same original seed to appear in multiple workers, producing duplicate episodes and GPU-count-dependent results.
- Fix: use the global `base_seed` (before offset) for the shuffle so every worker produces an identical ordering, then assign each worker a non-overlapping slice `[seed_offset * seeds_per_worker, (seed_offset+1) * seeds_per_worker)` of that globally-shuffled list.
- `self.base_seed` (= `cfg.seed`) is stored in `__init__` alongside the existing `self.seed` (= `cfg.seed + seed_offset`).

## Root cause

```python
# Before: each worker shuffles with a different seed → overlapping draws
self._generator.manual_seed(self.seed)  # self.seed differs per worker
shuffled_seeds = success_seeds[torch.randperm(..., generator=self._generator)]
self.success_seeds = shuffled_seeds[:keep_count]  # all start at index 0

# After: one canonical shuffle, then partition
global_generator.manual_seed(self.base_seed)  # same for all workers
shuffled_seeds = success_seeds[torch.randperm(..., generator=global_generator)]
worker_seeds = shuffled_seeds[start:end]  # non-overlapping slice
```

## Test plan

- [ ] With `total_num_envs=128` and 4 EnvWorkers, confirm all 128 seed slots map to unique original seeds (previously 105 unique / 23 duplicates per the issue).
- [ ] Single-worker runs unaffected: `seed_offset=0`, `total_num_processes=1` → `start=0`, `end=seeds_per_worker`, identical to the old full-list behavior.
- [ ] Deterministic: re-running with the same `env.eval.seed` produces the same per-worker partition.

result.title: RoboTwin eval may sample duplicate success_seeds across EnvWorkers
result.body:
## Problem

In RoboTwin evaluation, `env.eval.total_num_envs=128` is expected to evaluate 128 episodes / unseen seeds. However, the current seed selection logic appears to sample duplicate `success_seeds` across EnvWorkers.

Each EnvWorker loads the full `success_seeds` list, shuffles it independently with `env.eval.seed + seed_offset`, and then takes the first `num_group` seeds. Since each worker shuffles the full list independently, different workers can select overlapping seeds.

Relevant code:

```python
self._generator.manual_seed(self.seed)
shuffled_indices = torch.randperm(
    success_seeds.numel(), generator=self._generator
)
shuffled_seeds = success_seeds[shuffled_indices]
self.success_seeds = shuffled_seeds[:keep_count]
```

and later:

```python
indices = (
    torch.arange(self.num_group, device=self.success_seeds.device)
    + self._current_seed_index
) % total_seeds
reset_state_ids = self.success_seeds[indices]
```

`seed_offset` is per worker:

```python
seed_offset=self._rank * self.stage_num + stage_id
```

## Reproduction

Config:

```yaml
env:
  eval:
    total_num_envs: 128
    seed: 0
    group_size: 1
    use_fixed_reset_state_ids: true
    seeds_path: ${oc.env:REPO_PATH}/rlinf/envs/robotwin/seeds/eval_seeds.json
```

For `beat_block_hammer`, `eval_seeds.json` contains 320 `success_seeds`.

When running with 4 EnvWorkers, each worker gets 32 envs. I traced the actual `reset_state_ids` selected by each worker and got:

```text
total seeds = 128
unique seeds = 105
duplicate seed values = 22
extra duplicate occurrences = 23
```

Example duplicate seeds:

```text
100112514 appears 2 times
100150052 appears 3 times
100187513 appears 2 times
```

A local simulation of the current logic gives similar results:

```text
4 workers: total=128, unique=105
8 workers: total=128, unique=104
```

## Expected behavior

For evaluation, especially when reporting "128 unseen seeds", the selected reset seeds should probably be globally unique across all EnvWorkers, or at least the behavior should be documented clearly.

A more deterministic design may be:

1. Load `success_seeds` once logically.
2. Shuffle globally using `env.eval.seed`.
3. Partition by `seed_offset` / worker rank so different workers receive non-overlapping slices.
4. Keep the selected seed set independent of the number of visible GPUs if possible.

## Why this matters

The reported RoboTwin success rate depends on which seeds are evaluated. Duplicate seeds reduce the actual number of unique evaluation initial states and make results depend on EnvWorker count / visible GPUs.

result.title: feat(embodied): add LingBot-VA RoboTwin evaluation support
result.body:
### Description

This PR adds official LingBot-VA checkpoint support for RoboTwin evaluation in RLinf.

The main changes include:
- registering `lingbotva` as an embodied model in RLinf
- adding LingBot-VA rollout/evaluation integration on RoboTwin
- adding RoboTwin `ee` action support required by the official LingBot-VA inference workflow
- adding LingBot-VA install and asset download support
- adding Docker / install / embodied e2e / CI wiring for LingBot-VA on RoboTwin
- adding English and Chinese documentation pages for LingBot-VA evaluation

Current scope of this PR:
- RoboTwin evaluation only
- official LingBot-VA checkpoint inference only
- single-session evaluation per rollout worker
- `batch_size == 1`

This PR does **not** add SFT support for LingBot-VA yet.

### Motivation and Context

This change is required to integrate the official LingBot-VA RoboTwin checkpoint into RLinf, so that it can be loaded and evaluated inside RLinf's RoboTwin pipeline rather than only through the standalone upstream evaluation scripts.

The integration keeps the key model-side evaluation semantics required by LingBot-VA, including:
- 16D end-effector actions
- `add_init_pose`
- key-frame based chunk updates
- `compute_kv_cache` between chunks

At the same time, the implementation follows RLinf's embodied model conventions for config, install, docker, e2e, and documentation.

### How has this been tested?

Static checks:
- Python syntax checks passed for the LingBot-VA integration files via `py_compile`
- shell syntax checks passed for:
  - `requirements/install.sh`
  - `requirements/embodied/download_assets.sh`
  - `tests/e2e_tests/embodied/run_eval.sh`
- YAML parsing checks passed for:
  - `install.yml`
  - `docker-build.yml`
  - `embodied-e2e-tests.yml`
  - LingBot-VA example configs

- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed

Runtime validation:
- `bash requirements/install.sh embodied --model lingbotva --env robotwin`
- `bash requirements/embodied/download_assets.sh --assets lingbotva`
- RoboTwin evaluation smoke tests on the latest code:
  - `robotwin_click_bell_eval_lingbotva`: `eval/success_once = 1.0`
  - `robotwin_place_empty_cup_eval_lingbotva`: `eval/success_once = 1.0`

Notes on metrics:
- RLinf evaluation metrics are reported in RLinf's rollout aggregation format
- LingBot-VA is currently wired as RoboTwin evaluation only
- the evaluation configs keep `total_num_envs: 1` and `ignore_terminations: false`

result.title: feat: add lingbot vla to rlinf robotwin
result.body:
This PR introduces native integration of **LingBot-VLA** into the **RLinf + RoboTwin** embodied simulation ecosystem. Unlike the previous WebSocket-based communication, the model is now fully embedded into RLinf's Python memory space as a plugin, enabling zero-latency tensor-level interaction and efficient reinforcement learning fine-tuning (e.g., GRPO).

### Motivation

Prior to this PR, there was no support for LingBot's foundation model in RLinf’s evaluation and continuous training pipeline. Users had to rely on external HTTP services, which introduced overhead and limited scalability. This integration closes that gap by providing a seamless, high-performance native interface for LingBot-VLA, allowing it to be used directly in RLinf's embodied training and evaluation workflows.

### Key Changes

1. **Vision & Observation Pipeline** - Fixed visual grounding issues caused by SAPIEN’s `float32 [0,1]` images (which previously resulted in black frames).
* Aligned preprocessing with HTTP mode’s normalization (`bounds_99_woclip`) and exact channel transposition (`uint8` → `HWC` → `CHW` / 255.0).
* Unified global normalization keys (e.g., `action.arm.position`) from `robotwin_50.json` to enable seamless multi-task transfer without per-task overrides.


2. **Native Integration & GRPO Support** - Fully embedded LingBot-VLA into RLinf via a dedicated action model provider.
* Integrated Flow-SDE based action denoising with configurable `noise_method` (e.g., `flow_sde`), `noise_level`, and `num_steps`.


3. **Cluster Evaluation Runner Upgrade** - Patched `embodied_eval_runner.py` to inject an outer evaluation loop.
* Now supports true multi-episode cluster rollouts based on the `eval_episodes` Hydra argument, preventing premature termination after a single concurrency batch.


4. **Documentation & Configs** - Added LingBot-VLA to the official supported models matrix.
* Provided a quick-start integration guide in `README.md` and added dedicated YAML configuration files for both SFT and GRPO (e.g., `robotwin_click_bell_grpo_lingbotvla.yaml`).



---

### How to Test

Follow the steps below to verify the integration, from environment setup to training and evaluation.

#### 1. Clone RLinf and Install Dependencies

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RLinf/RLinf.git
cd RLinf
export RLINF_PATH=$(pwd)

# Install LingBot-VLA native environment and RoboTwin dependencies
bash requirements/install.sh embodied --model lingbotvla --env robotwin --use-mirror --no-root
source .venv/bin/activate

```

#### 2. Set Up RoboTwin Environment

```bash
cd ${RLINF_PATH}
git clone https://github.com/RoboTwin-Platform/RoboTwin.git -b RLinf_support
cd RoboTwin
export ROBOTWIN_PATH=$(pwd)
export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com
bash script/_download_assets.sh

```

#### 3. Download Model Weights

```bash
export LINGBOTVLA_PATH="${RLINF_PATH}/.venv/lingbot-vla"
cd ${LINGBOTVLA_PATH}

# Clone weights
git lfs install
git clone https://huggingface.co/robbyant/lingbot-vla-4b
git clone https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct

```

*Note: Before running the commands below, please ensure you have updated the `model_path` and `tokenizer_path` in the respective YAML configuration files to point to your local downloaded weights.*

#### 4. Test SFT (Behavior Cloning) Pipeline

Ensure the robot platform is set to ALOHA before launching, so the environment loads the 14-dimensional action space correctly:

```bash
export ROBOT_PLATFORM="ALOHA"
export REPO_PATH="${RLINF_PATH}"

bash examples/sft/run_vla_sft.sh robotwin_sft_lingbotvla

```

#### 5. Test GRPO Training Pipeline

```bash
export ROBOT_PLATFORM="ALOHA"
export REPO_PATH="${RLINF_PATH}"

bash examples/embodiment/run_embodiment.sh robotwin_click_bell_grpo_lingbotvla

```

#### 6. Test Evaluation Pipeline

```bash
export ROBOT_PLATFORM="ALOHA"
export REPO_PATH="${RLINF_PATH}"

bash examples/embodiment/eval_embodiment.sh robotwin_click_bell_grpo_lingbotvla_eval

```

Training logs can be monitored via TensorBoard:

```bash
tensorboard --logdir ../results --port 6006

```

### Description
This PR merges `release/v0.2` into `main`, bringing the complete RLinf v0.2 release scope, including:
- Major feature delivery for embodied and agentic/reasoning RL (e.g., real-world RL support, multi-agent training support, async training workflows, new model/env integrations).
- A set of bug fixes and stability improvements accumulated on `release/v0.2`.
- Documentation updates and link corrections across EN/ZH docs, including adding the new release notes page and updating tutorials index entries.
Key commits in this merge window include (non-exhaustive):
- `docs: add release notes (#936)`

result.title: feat: use uv hardlink mode for docker
result.body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
The symlink mode of uv is problematic in many aspects. For example, ray dashboard doesn't work when ray is installed via the symlink mode, as all the static assets of the ray dashboard server becomes symlink.

This PR changes docker to use the hardlink mode, which should have been the default mode of uv. result.title: perf: overlap bootstrap with training (cpu rendering)
result.body:
Performance Improvement: Asynchronous Environment Bootstrapping and Training Overlap

### Description
~~This PR introduces a new `warmup` method to the `EnvWorker` class to enable asynchronous environment preparation. The `warmup` function is designed to be called prior to `interact`, allowing environment bootstrapping to occur in parallel with `run_training`.
We also add a new `-1` configuration option for environment settings to explicitly denote CPU-only physics and rendering, and the function `get_group_accelerators` in `embodied_runner.py` to check if there is resource overlap.~~
Updated the PR based on feedback and copied suggested changes. Main difference is that warmup is not a function but an async handle (it is not called warmup anymore) and class member holding the bootstrap data is freed after consumption (e.g. set to `None`). 
There is also a new configuration for `runner`, `overlap_env_bootstrap`. This parameter needs to be set to True in the yaml file:
```
runner:
     overlap_env_bootstrap: True
``` 

### Motivation and Context
Currently, environment bootstrap time accounts for a significant portion (5%–20%) of each global step. In hardware configurations where `EnvWorker` processes do not compete for resources with the training actor (e.g., CPU-based rendering vs. NPU/GPU-based training), this bootstrap latency can be masked by overlapping it with the training phase.

While the initial global step time remains unchanged, subsequent steps see significant improvement in throughput.
*Preliminary Results:*
In a CPU + NPU environment (benchmarked on `libero_10` with Pi0.5 and PPO, with changes for minimal configuration), we observed a reduction in per-global-step time from 720s to approximately 620–640s.

### How has this been tested?
Validation is ongoing on our internal clusters using standard RLinf examples. Specifically:
Execution Script: `run_embodiment.sh`
Configuration: `libero_10_ppo_openpi_pi05.yaml` (with some selected minor adjustments from [Section 2.4 Minimum Test Case](https://rlinf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/rst_source/examples/embodied/pi0.html)).

### Additional information (optional, e.g., figures and logs):
Initial performance figures are posted in [comment](https://github.com/RLinf/RLinf/pull/942#issuecomment-4145842761).
_Further logs and performance figures will be attached upon completion of the test run._

result.title: [Bug]: requirements/install.sh的robotwin安装函数与nvcc --version输出结果的的适配问题
result.body:
### Affected component

robotwin的安装

### Bug description

requirements/install.sh脚本的557-558行
`
local cuda_major=$("$nvcc_exe" --version | grep 'Cuda compilation tools' | awk '{print $5}' | awk -F '.' '{print $1}')

local cuda_minor=$("$nvcc_exe" --version | grep 'Cuda compilation tools' | awk '{print $5}' | awk -F '.' '{print $2}')
`
假设 nvcc --version 输出中，Cuda compilation tools 行的第5个字段（以空格分隔）是纯数字版本号，例如：

`
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1 V12.1.105
`
但是我实际的nvcc --version输出
`
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105
`
在12.1末尾有逗号，这最终会导致安装curobo时报错
`
  × Failed to download and build `nvidia-curobo @
  │ git+https://github.com/NVlabs/curobo.git@ebb71702f3f70e767f40fd8e050674af0288abe8`
  ╰─▶ Package metadata version `0.0.0` does not match `0.7.7.post1.dev5` from
      the wheel filename
`
应该改为
`
    local cuda_major=$("$nvcc_exe" --version | grep 'Cuda compilation tools' | awk '{print $5}' | tr -d ',' | awk -F '.' '{print $1}')
    local cuda_minor=$("$nvcc_exe" --version | grep 'Cuda compilation tools' | awk '{print $5}' | tr -d ',' | awk -F '.' '{print $2}')
`
去掉逗号，来适配不同版本的nvcc的version输出格式

result.title: fix tactile memory leak problem

result.body: I had a similar issue before with H100 due to NVIDIA driver problems, which seems to be resolved in the latest NVIDIA driver. At the time, the issue only occurs when ray tracing is enabled (the driver reports that ray tracing is supported, but simply enabling ray tracing without even using it will break the whole renderer). If you are stuck on the current driver for whatever reason, you may try the environment variable `SAPIEN_DISABLE_RAY_TRACING=1` to see if it helps.

> 由于 NVIDIA 驱动程序问题，我之前在 H100 上遇到过类似的问题，这似乎在最新的 NVIDIA 驱动程序中得到了解决。目前，仅当启用光线追踪时，才会出现此问题（驱动程序报告支持光线追踪，但即使不使用光线追踪，也只是启用光线追踪会破坏整个渲染器）。如果您出于任何原因卡在当前驱动程序上，您可以尝试环境变量以查看是否有帮助。`SAPIEN_DISABLE_RAY_TRACING=1`

I see. I think the best solution is avoiding using sapien in H20 / H100. 😂
